name: Tanegashima Yoshinobu LP-1
best_known_for: Japan's heavy-lift gateway — H-IIA + H3, HTV / HTV-X cargo to the ISS
credit: Yoshinobu Launch Complex at the Tanegashima Space Center on Japan's southern island. Original H-II first flight August 1996; H-IIA from 2001 (a workhorse with a 49-out-of-50 success rate); HTV cargo to the ISS from 2009 to 2020; HTV-X from 2025 onward. LP-1 was upgraded for the new H3 in 2023. Tanegashima's 30°N latitude is workable for geostationary launches with the southern Pacific corridor downrange. Coordinates from JAXA fact sheets.
